tldr: Survey responses from 30+ Oregonians (business owners, workers, non-profits, consultants) about barriers to state prosperity. Dominant themes: workforce development and education costs, housing affordability and homelessness, business taxation (QSBS, CAT, CPP) and permitting complexity, public transit funding, health-care-employment decoupling, and need for coordinated state vision. Respondents span workforce issues, business climate, and tools-for-growth categories.

bullets.text: 81% of 200 Central Oregon employers surveyed by Bend Chamber cite housing as #1 barrier to worker attraction and retention; 30% of regional workforce rent-burdened, 50% severely rent-burdened
Multiple business respondents (Paxbytes, Ear Trumpet Labs, Generation Solar, Jordan Rice) cite QSBS tax treatment, CAT, and CPP as disincentives to starting or growing businesses in Oregon

Workforce respondents (Chris Bloome, Steven Demarest, Steve Salman, Cindi Dale) advocate mandating Career Technical Education (CTE) in high schools within 4–5 years and reducing community college/higher education costs
Lamb Weston (1000+ employees) warns that layered regulations (air, wastewater, CAT, CPP) and unclear compliance metrics are unsustainable in competitive global markets and risk business relocation
Aaron Johnson (98683) proposes natural systems science (oceanography, forestry, climate data) as economic development anchor, citing Oregon's coastal research institutions and data assets
Susan Bladholm (Frog Ferry) and multiple respondents flag public agency culture as barrier: lack of responsiveness to private-sector input, closed-door decision-making, and accountability gaps
Anonymous respondent (97202) expresses disappointment that Council survey was poorly distributed and excludes working-class voices; advocates universal preschool and Oregon Health Plan expansion
Rob Bennett proposes statewide tax overhaul: introducing modest sales tax, reducing corporate and individual income tax rates, and addressing property tax restrictions via constitutional amendment
